snapshot: WHO African Region. Africa's most populous country hosts the 5th Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR in Abuja (6 to 8 December) and votes for president on 16 January 2027. It signed the US health agreement with the largest co-investment so far, and contained its first imported Ebola (Bundibugyo) case in October and November 2026.

agenda.title: Hosting the AMR ministerial in Abuja
agenda.text: The 5th Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR (6 to 8 December, Transcorp Hilton, Abuja) is the first on African soil, themed 'One Health: Advancing Global AMR Commitments through Local Action'. Four ministries co-lead it and it should adopt an Abuja Compact on AMR. The minister has acknowledged gaps in Nigeria's own AMR surveillance, laboratory capacity and financing.

agenda.title: The US health agreement
agenda.text: Signed on 19 December 2025 for April 2026 to December 2030: the US puts in about US$2.1 billion and Nigeria raises domestic health spending by about US$3 billion, the largest co-investment under the America First strategy, and commits to at least 6% of its budget for health. The US says it includes dedicated funding for Christian health facilities. Its data and specimen-sharing terms drew scrutiny in October; Ghana rejected a similar compact.

agenda.title: Ebola: one imported case, contained
agenda.text: A traveller from Uganda, via Addis Ababa, was confirmed with Bundibugyo virus on 20 October and evacuated to Switzerland. All 62 contacts completed 21 days of monitoring by 13 November without a new case. NCDC had rated the import risk high since May and put states on alert.

agenda.title: Paying for health
agenda.text: The proposed 2026 health budget of ₦2.48 trillion is the largest in naira but about 4.2% of the federal budget, short of the 6% the minister aimed for and now committed under the US agreement. Insurance expansion through the NHIA and the Basic Health Care Provision Fund remain the main routes to financial protection.

agenda.title: Lassa fever, diphtheria and other outbreaks
agenda.text: Lassa fever spread to 18 states early in the year, with health workers among the infected. Diphtheria remains large: 8,604 confirmed cases in the first 27 weeks of 2026 against 6,127 a year earlier, although the case fatality rate fell from 6.2% to 2.3%. Cholera and mpox are also active incidents.

nl.text: The Netherlands and Nigeria signed an agreement on an autologous blood service in March 2024. PharmAccess, based in Amsterdam, is the Dutch government's implementing partner for health in Nigeria, working on health insurance and quality of care. Further links come from the NPHI Collaboration Map.

items.title: Agreement on tackling blood shortages (autologous blood service)
items.who: Nigerian Federal Ministry of Health, the Netherlands (Deputy Minister for Public Health), National Blood Service Commission and HemoClear
items.text: Sets up a service that processes a patient's own blood during surgery so it can be transfused back, to ease shortages and keep donated blood for conditions such as sickle cell disease and cancer. The partnership is financed by the French Fund for Innovation in Development.

items.title: PharmAccess: Dutch-funded health insurance and quality programmes
items.who: PharmAccess Foundation with the National Health Insurance Authority and state governments such as Delta
items.when: ongoing; Dutch healthcare business delegation in April 2024
items.text: Through the Health Insurance Fund the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs supports health insurance and private-sector capacity for low- and middle-income groups; PharmAccess implements Dutch health activities in Nigeria.

timeline.text: Five-year US–Nigeria health MoU signed under the America First strategy.
INEC moves the presidential election forward to 16 January 2027.
NCDC raises the alarm over Lassa fever in 18 states, including among health workers.
AMR ministerial moved from June to 6 to 8 December.
NCDC rates the Ebola import risk high and puts ten states on alert.
Presidential and National Assembly campaigns open.
Daily Trust reports the data and specimen-sharing terms of the US agreement.
First imported Ebola (Bundibugyo) case confirmed in Abuja.
All 62 Ebola contacts complete monitoring without a new case.

brief.lead: Nigeria comes to the AMR ministerial as host and agenda-setter, a few weeks before national elections. Health sovereignty, financing and local vaccine research are the minister's themes.

points.text: AMR: the Abuja Compact is the deliverable. Dutch strengths in One Health surveillance and stewardship match the gaps the minister himself names in surveillance and laboratory capacity.

Financing: the US agreement binds Nigeria to at least 6% of the budget for health, while the 2026 proposal was about 4.2%. Dutch experience with insurance through PharmAccess and the NHIA is a relevant asset.
Health security: NCDC contained the imported Ebola case and traced all contacts, which makes it a credible partner on preparedness and cross-border surveillance.

careful.text: Elections on 16 January 2027 (governors on 6 February): agendas and people may change after the vote, so avoid commitments that depend on continuity.
The faith-based funding and the data and specimen-sharing terms of the US agreement are sensitive at home; Ghana rejected a similar deal.
Lassa fever infections among health workers are a sore point for the profession.

ask: What will the Abuja Compact ask of high-income countries, and how will follow-up be tracked?
How do the specimen and data-sharing terms of the US agreement fit Nigeria's position in the WHO pathogen access and benefit-sharing (PABS) negotiations?
